# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 21 (Bu-Vb Np21)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Np21
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 21
**Title (English, from literature):** Keeping an extra almsbowl beyond ten days
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-np21
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 21 (*Patta*) is the twenty-first rule in the forfeiture category of the Pali *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a Buddhist monk who keeps an extra almsbowl for more than ten days commits an offense; he must relinquish the excess bowl and formally confess the transgression [SuttaCentral].
This training rule is widespread across Buddhist monastic traditions. SuttaCentral identifies parallels in the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra*, as well as in the Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣas preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan belonging to the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahāsāṃghika (and Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravādin) traditions [SuttaCentral]. Akira Hirakawa notes that in the parallel Mahāsāṃghika rule (NP 21), monastics are permitted only one bowl, and keeping excess bowls constitutes a violation [Hirakawa 1982]. DharmaNexus aligns sections of the Pali text with the Tibetan translation of the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (with similarity scores reaching 95), along with the *Vinayasaṃgraha*, the Sanskrit *Pravāraṇāvastu*, and the *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* [DharmaNexus].
Pali-internal text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus document 1,209 shared passages across 138 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Substantial legal and formulaic overlap occurs with other *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* rules—most prominently the first robe rule of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Bu-Vb Np1) and *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Bi-Vb Np1), as well as Bu-Vb Np19, Np22, and Np23 [DharmaNexus]. Significant textual reuse is also detected with Khandhaka treatises (including the *Samuccayakkhandhaka*, *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka*, *Mahākhandhaka*, and *Cīvarakkhandhaka*) and Vinaya commentarial literature, such as the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā*, *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
